reply.recognition: Recognized as UCI Parkinson's Telemonitoring (UCI 189) from the supplied documentation; no remembered prior-study result is claimed or used.
reply.summary: The input describes 5,875 home voice recordings nested in 42 people over about six months, with interpolated motor and total UPDRS targets. I select a paired-replicate measurement study asking whether apparent within-person voice change is repeatable enough to guide monitoring. This adds a testable measurement and decision design beyond score prediction; it is proposal-only, not a clinical-validity finding.

candidates.title: Replicate-aware voice change alerts
candidates.question: For a remote-monitoring session, does averaging three standardized home voice recordings improve detection of clinically anchored within-person motor change compared with one recording, at the same false-alert rate?
candidates.new_claim: A replicate-based session estimate may separate short-term recording variability from persistent voice change enough to improve alert reliability; this is a proposal, not a finding in the supplied data.
candidates.input_delta: Adds same-session repeats, a fixed aggregation rule, and clinical alert comparison. Supplied rows lack replicate/session identifiers and a controlled repeat protocol.
candidates.domain_value: Helps decide whether one voice capture is adequate or a second/third should be requested before acting on a change alert.
assumptions: Motor status is effectively unchanged during a replicate set collected minutes apart.
Prompt, microphone position, and recording procedure can be maintained at home.
The clinical comparison uses independently observed motor UPDRS assessments; interpolated labels are not independent observations.
A clinically meaningful score change and alert threshold are prespecified before validation.
candidates.variables_and_units: Independent unit: participant, with sessions nested within participant. Collect three recordings per session using the same prompt/setup; compare one recording with the arithmetic mean of three. Acoustic feature units are unspecified in the supplied documentation. Record follow-up time in days and observed clinician motor UPDRS in score points. Outcomes: within-session feature dispersion and held-out sensitivity at a fixed false-alert rate for a prespecified clinically meaningful score change.
candidates.testable_prediction: In participant-held-out validation, the three-recording mean will have lower within-session acoustic dispersion and higher sensitivity for prespecified observed motor-UPDRS change than one recording, at the same false-alert rate.
candidates.alternative: Replicate differences mostly reflect real short-term symptom or medication-state fluctuation; averaging removes useful signal and does not improve or worsens detection of clinical change.
candidates.discriminating_test: Collect three fixed-task recordings minutes apart at each home session, repeat over follow-up, and obtain observed clinician motor-UPDRS assessments at prespecified visits. Split validation by participant; compare alert sensitivity for one recording versus the three-recording mean at the same prespecified false-alert rate, with participant-level uncertainty. Freeze score-change threshold and aggregation rule before validation.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Only a sampling-density check is feasible: summarize within-person test_time gaps. No same-session repeatability, error attribution, or clinical alert validation is possible because replicate/session IDs and independently observed UPDRS labels at every recording are absent.
candidates.required_new_data: Prospective sessions with three same-task recordings minutes apart, setup metadata, repeated sessions per participant, and time-aligned independently observed clinician motor-UPDRS scores at clinical visits; record medication timing/state as an alternative explanation.
candidates.failure_condition: Unsupported for this use if the mean fails to reduce within-session dispersion or improve held-out sensitivity at equal false-alert rate, or if benefit disappears under participant-held-out validation.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query for Parkinson home/remote voice studies directly comparing single recordings with same-session replicate aggregation for test-retest reliability or clinically anchored change alerts.

candidates.title: Separate medication-state response from progression
candidates.question: Do within-person voice measurements distinguish acute clinician-confirmed medication ON/OFF motor state from slower progression?
candidates.new_claim: A within-person voice signature might track acute motor-state changes separately from slower baseline trajectory; medication timing and ON/OFF status are absent from supplied variables.
candidates.input_delta: Adds timed medication-state labels and paired clinical assessments, changing the target from interpolated-score prediction to separation of acute state response from longitudinal change.
candidates.domain_value: Could prevent an acute medication fluctuation from being interpreted as disease progression and guide dose-aligned voice follow-up.
assumptions: Clinician-confirmed ON/OFF state can be measured alongside voice in the same participant.
Task, time of day, and setup can be held stable or recorded.
Any voice composite and its direction are frozen before participant-held-out validation.
candidates.variables_and_units: Participant-level paired ON/OFF sessions; categorical clinician-confirmed medication state; elapsed time since dose in hours; acoustic features in documented units (unspecified); observed motor UPDRS in score points; follow-up time in days. Compare within-person ON/OFF voice-feature differences with matched same-state temporal pairs.
candidates.testable_prediction: A composite defined in discovery participants will show a reproducible within-person association with observed motor-UPDRS difference across ON/OFF pairs in held-out participants, beyond matched same-state pairs and follow-up time.
candidates.alternative: Voice variation is dominated by recording/task variation or slower disease differences and has no stable acute state signal after within-person pairing.
candidates.discriminating_test: Collect repeated voice and observed motor-UPDRS assessments in confirmed ON/OFF states with fixed task/setup; match same-state comparisons by time of day and follow-up interval; validate the frozen composite by participant. The supplied dataset has no medication-state field and cannot test medication effects.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No direct medication-state test: dose timing and ON/OFF labels are absent.
candidates.required_new_data: Repeated voice captures paired with confirmed ON/OFF state, dose and elapsed-time metadata, observed motor scores, and standardized task/setup and time-of-day records.
candidates.failure_condition: Fails if the frozen composite does not distinguish ON/OFF motor-score changes from matched same-state variation in held-out participants, or if association is accounted for by time or recording conditions.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query for paired Parkinson medication ON/OFF studies using repeated home/remote voice measurements and observed motor scores.

candidates.title: Use voice variability to trigger symptom check-ins
candidates.question: Does within-day voice variability identify patient-reported motor-fluctuation episodes well enough to trigger an extra check-in more efficiently than fixed-time sampling?
candidates.new_claim: Within-day acoustic dispersion may signal a fluctuating symptom day rather than only poor recording quality; a burden-matched trigger policy can test whether it helps remote follow-up.
candidates.input_delta: Adds repeated daily recordings and contemporaneous symptom reports, evaluating a sampling decision rather than UPDRS score prediction.
candidates.domain_value: Could request extra symptom assessment selectively on likely fluctuation days while preserving event detection at lower monitoring burden.
assumptions: Patients can provide time-stamped fluctuation reports with adequate completion.
Recordings and reports can be scheduled within day; medication timing and setup are recorded.
Check-in burden can be represented by counts per participant-week.
candidates.variables_and_units: Decision unit: participant-day, with recordings nested within participant and day. Collect morning and later-day samples; calculate within-day dispersion of a prespecified voice composite. Record fluctuation event as time-stamped categorical patient report and check-ins as counts. Compare event detection at equal check-in counts per participant-week.
candidates.testable_prediction: At equal check-in count per participant-week, a frozen high-dispersion trigger will detect more patient-reported fluctuation days than fixed-time sampling in held-out participants.
candidates.alternative: Dispersion is mostly caused by setup or medication timing and does not track reported fluctuations; fixed-time sampling performs as well or better.
candidates.discriminating_test: Collect time-stamped repeated home recordings, brief symptom reports, medication timing, and setup metadata. Freeze a dispersion threshold in development data, then compare event sensitivity at matched check-in burden against fixed sampling in held-out participants; account for repeated participant-days.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No direct policy test: the table has no same-day marker, symptom diary, medication timing, or check-in outcomes.
candidates.required_new_data: Multiple daily recordings, contemporaneous fluctuation reports, medication timing/state, setup metadata, and check-in burden/outcome in a prospective cohort.
candidates.failure_condition: Unsupported if the trigger does not detect more fluctuation days than fixed sampling at matched burden in participant-held-out evaluation, or if the signal is explained by setup or medication timing.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query for Parkinson home voice monitoring using within-day acoustic variability to trigger symptom assessment or adaptive sampling at matched monitoring burden.

task.deliverable: Critique I1 and return a tightened protocol-ready measurement design. Preserve its prediction and explicit alternative until any broker result returns. Identify that existing data can check sampling density only, not repeatability or clinical validity.
acceptance: State the primary estimand, independent unit, comparison, and fixed alert operating point.
Address real short-term symptom/medication change versus recording variability and name minimum metadata to distinguish them.
If useful, request at most one computation of per-person recording-pair counts with absolute test_time gaps <=1 day and <=7 days; interpret only as schedule feasibility.
If useful, request at most one Crossref search on same-session replicate voice measurement and clinically anchored change detection; report query and search-coverage limits.
Keep proposal-only absent direct supporting evidence; do not treat interpolated UPDRS as independent clinical observations or claim literature novelty without supporting comparison.
task.proposed_computation: Potential broker check: for each participant summarize counts of recording pairs with absolute test_time gap <=1 day and <=7 days, plus participant-level counts. This checks schedule density only; it cannot separate biological fluctuation from measurement error or validate clinical alerts.
task.proposed_search: Potential single Crossref query: (Parkinson OR Parkinson's) AND (voice OR speech) AND (home OR remote) AND (repeatability OR test-retest OR replicate) AND (clinical change OR motor score). Seek direct comparison of single versus repeated same-session recordings with a clinical change anchor; titles alone do not establish methods or findings.
